domain: Artificial Intelligence / Consumer Robotics / Surveillance & Privacy

slides.headline: Ring’s Cameras Will Roam Your Rooms.
slides.subheadline: The privacy promise has a catch.
slides.body: Flying and rolling cameras bring autonomous patrols inside. Understand the mapping, recording and encryption trade-offs before buying.​

slides.headline: Three Things To Know Before Buying
bullets: Both devices map interiors using AI Pilot, combining vision models, on-device sensors and cloud processing.
Drone flights last up to 8 minutes, tested with a new, fully-charged battery under controlled conditions.
Rover cloud recordings can remain for up to 180 days with a compatible Ring subscription.

slides.headline: One Flies. One Rolls. Both Map.

cards.title: DRONE CAM
cards.body: 2K video, 148° field of view, 360° rotation and two LED lights for low-light scenes.

cards.title: ROVER CAM
cards.body: Adjustable periscope; up to 4K livestreaming and recording during patrols; 360° scans at designated stops.

cards.title: SETUP
cards.body: Carry Drone through your rooms; Rover explores independently. AI Pilot creates floor plans and suggests patrol points.

slides.headline: Two Prices. One Long Recording Window.

cards.title: DRONE CAM
cards.body: U.S. shipping targeted January 27, 2027. FCC authorization remains pending; sales cannot proceed without approval.

cards.title: ROVER CAM
cards.body: Business-focused robot available for preorder. U.S. shipping scheduled for December 16, 2026.

cards.title: ROVER CLOUD RETENTION
cards.body: Doorbell rings, motion events and Live View recordings; compatible subscription required. Not continuous recording.

slides.headline: Amazon Promises Privacy. Its Record Demands Scrutiny.

cards.title: AMAZON’S PROMISE
cards.body: “Privacy and security without compromise”: docked Drone camera off; Rover Sleep Mode retracts its periscope and disables its microphone.

cards.title: CIVIL-LIBERTIES WARNING
cards.body: EFF says TAKE falls short of end-to-end encryption and leaves potential avenues for compelled access.

cards.title: PAST SECURITY FAILURES
cards.body: The FTC’s 2023 complaint said vulnerabilities exposed approximately 55,000 U.S. customers’ videos, live streams and account profiles.

cards.title: INSIDER ACCESS
cards.body: The FTC also charged Ring with allowing employees and contractors to access customers’ private videos.

slides.headline: The Catch: Cloud Processing, Subscriptions, Temporary Keys

cards.title: NOT LOCAL-ONLY
cards.body: AI Pilot combines interior mapping with cloud processing—not exclusively on-device computation.

cards.title: AUTOMATION COSTS EXTRA
cards.body: Scheduled Drone flights and Rover patrols require a compatible Ring Protect plan.

cards.title: TAKE IS NOT END-TO-END
cards.body: EFF says Throw Away the Key Encryption permits cloud decryption for 24 hours before Ring deletes its keys.

cards.title: KEYS CAN RETURN
cards.body: Viewing older footage or using smart features can send keys back to Ring’s servers, EFF explains.

cards.reality: Up to 8 minutes per flight; tested with a new, fully-charged battery under controlled conditions. Then it recharges.
Claimed coverage: up to 5,000 sq ft. Indoor, single-floor operation only; it cannot climb stairs.
Incompatible: transitions greater than 1.375 inches/3.5cm, curved edges, sunken areas and black glossy floors.

slides.headline: Privacy First? Skip Both. Otherwise, Wait.

cards.title: AVOID
cards.body: Privacy-first buyers: neither product’s cloud-dependent design meets a local-only requirement.

cards.title: POTENTIAL FIT
cards.body: Consider only after independent testing: homeowners needing brief checks or businesses with compatible, single-floor interiors.

cards.title: WRONG EXPECTATIONS
cards.body: Avoid Drone for sustained airborne coverage; avoid Rover if your security plan requires navigating stairs.​

slides.headline: The Camera Is Becoming A Mobile Investigator

cards.title: FROM WATCHING TO RESPONDING
cards.body: Connected Ring alerts can dispatch either device to preset patrol points—not merely trigger a stationary recording.

cards.title: FROM VIDEO TO FLOOR PLANS
cards.body: AI Pilot adds mapped rooms, suggested viewpoints and autonomous routing to indoor monitoring.

cards.title: THE BIGGER QUESTION
cards.body: Editorial takeaway: evaluate access controls and independent verification as closely as camera resolution.

slides.headline: More Visibility Is Not Automatically More Privacy.
slides.body: Our verdict: wait for independent testing. Mobility is a capability—not proof that the privacy promise holds.
slides.question: Would you let a cloud-connected camera map and patrol your private rooms?
slides.cta: Where would you draw the line?
